cross-package @primeuix/* import specifiers rewritten to @ultimate/uix-* via scripts/provenance/adapt-imports.mjs; removed one obsolete, rule-free eslint-disable-next-line directive during GAP-092 lint repair (comment only, no runtime change); A1 (#171): the empty `@todo` update() (identical in the upstream @primeuix/styled src/stylesheet/index.ts:49-51) is replaced by update(key, css), which rewrites a registered entry in place and writes through the new updateStyleElement(element, meta) hook; the entry shape reuses add()'s. The remaining members are unchanged, so the class stays COPY. A3 (#173): add(key, css, options) and update(key, css, options) take an optional `first` flag, and StyleMeta carries it to createStyleElement. A first entry is moved to the front of the registry order (so getAllCSS and getAllMarkup list it first) and its element is created at the start of its container. The `first` option mirrors the `first: true` option of PrimeVue 4.5.5 UseStyle.js:30,57 and PrimeNG 21.1.9 usestyle.ts:16,29, which differs in form (a loader option, not a registry method) and shares only the behavior. The upstream class is untouched elsewhere, so the class stays COPY.

Ultimate-owned, framework-agnostic reimplementation of PrimeVue BaseComponent's _loadThemeStyles() two-tier theme-variable loading (common primitive/semantic/global tier loaded once globally; per-component variable tier loaded once per component name, both idempotently guarded). Reshaped from PrimeVue's Vue-component-method form into a plain function taking a uix-styled StyleSheet, so ng-core/react-core/vue-core can each drive it from their own existing structural-CSS registration call site. Excludes PrimeVue's isUnstyled/$theme==='none' short-circuits and its BaseStyle/$styleOptions indirection. A1 (#171): the module now keeps each sheet's variable blocks current after theme:change, and adds registerComponentCss, which registers a component's structural CSS and re-renders it after theme:change because dt() bakes the variable prefix into it. Compared side by side with the pinned archives (ADR-064): PrimeVue 4.5.5 BaseComponent.vue (_themeChangeListener, _load) and PrimeNG 21.1.9 basecomponent.ts (_themeChangeListener) share only the interface facts (the theme:change event name, ThemeService.on/off, rerunning the variable loading). The per-sheet WeakMap, the WeakRef-held subscription and registerComponentCss are Ultimate-authored; no upstream wording, statements or structure is retained, so the class stays REFERENCE. F4 (ticket #172) adds the common tier's global style: the preset's top-level `css` is registered under `u-global-style` through Theme.transformCSS, after the common variables, as PrimeVue 4.5.5 BaseComponent.vue:170-175 and PrimeNG 21.1.9 basecomponent.ts:355-360 load their `global-style` entry. Ultimate does not prepend the @primeuix/styles base `style` that those loaders also include: it is page-wide, ADR-063 scopes the equivalent box-model rule per component, and the uix-styles/base direction belongs to F10 (ticket A6). F7 (ticket #174) reads a component's preset block under its registration name with the hyphens removed (`input-text` reads `inputtext`), in one private helper used by the first registration and by the theme:change rewrite alike; the block stays registered under the name it was given. Upstream has no counterpart: PrimeNG 21.1.9 and PrimeVue 4.5.5 components register under the flat Aura key itself (ADR-051), so there is nothing to normalize there. The helper is Ultimate-authored and the class stays REFERENCE. F6 (ticket #173) registers the `@layer` order statement from Theme.getLayerOrderCSS() under `u-layer-order`, first in the sheet, after the common and component variable blocks have recorded their layer names, and again on theme:change. Compared side by side with the pinned archives (ADR-064): PrimeNG 21.1.9 basecomponent.ts:375-381 and PrimeVue 4.5.5 BaseComponent.vue:191-197 (and BaseDirective.js:119-125) load a `layer-order` style with `first: true` once per loaded-style cycle, built by BaseStyle getLayerOrderThemeCSS (basestyle.ts:78-80, BaseStyle.js:60-62). Only the interface facts are shared: the Theme.getLayerOrderCSS call, the `first` placement and the order-after-variables sequence. Ultimate's syncLayerOrder compares the computed statement with the registered one instead of a loaded-name sentinel, so a function-valued cssLayer.order that depends on later-recorded layer names is refreshed, and a cssLayer switched on or off at runtime updates the existing entry. No upstream wording, statements or structure is retained, so the class stays REFERENCE. PrimeReact 10.9.9 has no counterpart: searching components/lib for getLayerOrder, layer-order and cssLayer finds only the `@layer primereact` rule hard-coded in componentbase/ComponentBase.js:260 and in the component Base.js style strings. F15 (ticket #175): the private presetKey helper is now exported inside the package (not from the barrel) so createScopedTheme reads the preset under the same hyphen-free name.

Ultimate-owned, framework-agnostic helper for per-instance dt (F15, ticket #175). Reference: PrimeVue 4.5.5 BaseComponent.vue (`_loadScopedThemeStyles`, `_unloadScopedThemeStyles`, the dt watcher) and PrimeNG 21.1.9 basecomponent.ts (same names). Compared side by side with the pinned archives (ADR-064): they share only interface facts (Theme.getCustomPreset with a `[<attrSelector>]` selector, the `<attrSelector>-<name>` registry key, rerunning on theme:change). The factory with update() and dispose(), the hyphen-free preset name through presetKey, the StyleSheet-based writes, and removing the style element together with the registry entry (StyleSheet.delete() alone leaves the element in the document) are Ultimate-authored; no upstream wording, statements or structure is retained, so the class is REFERENCE. The upstream methods are bound to a Vue or Angular component instance; this one takes a StyleSheet so ng-core and vue-core share it.
